children: Commercial vehicle volumes increase 32 per cent to 64,677 units; company reports record quarterly volumes, revenue and profit

Ashok Leyland reported a 39 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 13,364 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by higher commercial vehicle volumes and improved realisations. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 13 per cent to Rs 869 crore, compared with Rs 771 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company recorded commercial vehicle volumes of 64,677 units during the quarter, a 32 per cent increase from 49,116 units in Q2 FY26. Profit before tax (PBT) grew 14 per cent to Rs 1,187 crore from Rs 1,043 crore.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs 1,350 crore, compared with Rs 1,162 crore a year earlier. However, the EBITDA margin declined to 10.1 per cent from 12.1 per cent in the year-ago quarter.
MHCV Volumes Grow 44%, Market Share Improves

Medium and heavy commercial vehicle (MHCV) volumes increased 44 per cent year-on-year to 37,958 units, compared with 26,307 units in Q2 FY26. This was higher than the industry's growth of 39 per cent.
Light commercial vehicle (LCV) volumes rose 21 per cent to 21,371 units from 17,697 units. Domestic MHCV truck volumes increased 48 per cent, outpacing industry growth of 41 per cent.

Ashok Leyland reported a domestic truck market share of 31.5 per cent, gaining 1.5 percentage points during the quarter, excluding defence. Its LCV market share in addressable segments improved to 13.6 per cent. Export volumes increased 7 per cent to 5,102 units.

The company ended the quarter with net cash of Rs 3,546 crore, compared with Rs 990 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its board declared an interim dividend of Rs 1 per share, equivalent to 100 per cent of the face value.
